newsitem.title: USA: Small oil, gas producers seek open US power market.
newsitem.headline: Small oil, gas producers seek open US power market.

text.p: U.S. independent oil and natural gas producers said Tuesday that one of their top priorities this year would be to press state and federal lawmakers to open power markets to competition.

Members of the Independent Petroleum Association of America said they wanted competitive power markets across the country because they are big consumers of electricity and producers of natural gas, one of the major fuels used to generate power.
"Electricity is a very large part of our costs," said George Yates, an independent producer and IPAA vice chairman. Power market competition could help cut those costs.

New demand for electricity could double natural gas use from 3.5 trillion cubic feet burned today for electricity, if clean air rules were tightened to make coal-fired power plants meet the same pollution limits as gas-fired plants, IPAA said.
Yates said the government could change those rules, but he did not specify how it might be done without reopening the Clean Air Act, a law he called "affirmative action for coal."
"We want a comprehensiveness in the restructuring that will allow natural gas to compete fairly for the electricity market," he said at a news conference.
IPAA officials said they wanted all states to open their electricity markets to competition by some deadline, but they did not know what date that should be.
A Republican proposal in the U.S. House seeks to make all states open their markets by the end of 2000.

Yates said it was important for independent producers to be actively involved in shaping the growing debate on power markets, even though they were still recovering from battles over natural gas market deregulation.
"We know if we're not involved, somebody's going to eat our lunch," he said.
IPAA officials were more optimistic about their industry than they have been over the last several years.
"After more than a decade of low prices, declining production, job losses and bankruptcies, some positive things are happening across the country," said IPAA chairman Lew Ward.
